title: Gear and Load

sections.heading: The Kit and the character sheet
paragraphs: K opens the Kit: everything you carry, sorted by kind, each piece set beside the one you wear. @ opens your character sheet. On either one, pick a piece and press:
rows: Wear or wield it, or take it off
Ready a weapon (it hangs at your back), or put it back in your pack
Apply a coating to the weapon in your hand, or put the earplugs in or take them out
Identify it (you need the Philosopher's Shard)

sections.heading: Apply puts the earplugs in
paragraphs: Beeswax Earplugs do nothing in your pack. Press A on them in the Kit and the wax goes in: no voice can work on you then, not a wail's fear, a song's sleep or a scream's confusion. But you hear nothing either, so press A again to take them out once the singing stops.

sections.heading: A readied weapon
paragraphs: Ready a weapon from the Kit (R) and it hangs at your back, readied. S swaps it with the weapon in your hand in one turn, so you can change weapons in the middle of a fight. A two-handed weapon sends your shield to your pack; swap back to a one-handed weapon and the shield goes back on your arm in the same turn. Drop it or throw it and it keeps its place: pick it up again and S draws it.

sections.heading: Three Loadouts
paragraphs: Shift+E opens your Loadouts: three saved kits. Dress as you like, pick a kit (1, 2 or 3) and press S to save what you wear into it, and N to give it a name. Enter puts a kit on. Only the pieces that change take time: each shows its turns beside it (taking off what is in its way counted in), with the total for the whole change. A piece not in your pack is skipped, and one you have never worn stays off until you have put it on by hand.

sections.heading: Putting armour on
paragraphs: The first time you put on a kind of armour, a shield, a ring or an amulet, it asks its questions. After that the kind is Known by Hand: every iron breastplate goes on with no quiz, whatever its plus or blessing, though a mithril one is a new kind and asks its own. A ring or amulet is known up to the strongest you have worn: a Ring of Protection V asks its own questions once, even after a Ring of Protection I, but a weaker one goes straight on.
Get a question wrong and you struggle with the piece for as long as it takes to put on, then give up: those turns are lost, and the monsters have them.

Armour takes time. Light body armour goes on in 1 turn, medium in 3, heavy in 5 and full plate in 6; every other piece takes 1, and taking a piece off takes half as long. A piece does nothing for you until it is fully on.
If a foe comes into view or strikes you while you dress, you stop and the game asks: Keep dressing? Y keeps going. N stops: what is on stays on, and the rest stays in your pack.

sections.heading: Coatings, flasks and stance
paragraphs: Three keys get you ready for what is in front of you:
rows: Coat the weapon in your hand with silver dust, holy water, fire oil, frost salts or venom. It lasts for a number of blows that land, and against a creature that cannot bear it (silver on a werewolf) every one of them strikes its weakness
Throw: the Flasks tab holds oil, holy water and acid, which burst over the creature they hit
Change your stance, one turn: Press hits 30% harder but leaves you 2 AC worse, Guard hits 30% softer but makes you 2 AC better, and Neutral is in between

sections.heading: How much you carry
paragraphs: Strength sets how much you can carry, and everything counts, worn or packed. You can never pick up more than your limit, and the moment you lighten your load its cost lifts. The sidebar shows your load:
rows: Over half your limit: you dodge half as well, and your footsteps carry further
Over three quarters: you cannot dodge, your Dexterity guards you half as well, and every second step costs an extra turn
Past the limit itself (losing Strength can put you there): you cannot dodge, your Dexterity no longer guards you, and every step costs an extra turn

sections.heading: A Bococho's saddlebags, and riding her
paragraphs: A Bococho who has chosen you wears saddlebags. While she is out with you they carry 20 lb of your load, so your limit and every line above it (Heavy, Burdened, Overloaded) move up by 20. Put her in her sphere and the bags go with her.

Once she is grown, you can ride her. With no foe in sight and her beside you, press Shift+R (or M on her card in the pet menu) to climb into the saddle, and again to climb down. In the saddle each step covers two tiles, but the dungeon's time passes as it always does: one turn for each move.

She sets you down at once when a foe comes into view, when something strikes you, when a trap or the floor itself catches her, when you start anything that asks a question (a blow, a spell, a wand), at the stairs (she follows you), when you are stunned, confused, asleep or held, and when your load is too heavy for her. Her big running feet are loud: things hear you coming from further off.
